Detroit: Become Human is a game that is many things. While you'll be experiencing it all as an android, it allows you to feel like Neo from "The Matrix", Andy Dufresne from "The Shawshank Redemption" and sometimes even Murtaugh from "Lethal Weapon". It borrows heavily from pop culture and actual history but if you're okay with that you'll be treated to a cinematic and emotional experience with top notch graphics, voice acting and music.

While, yes, a David Cage game like this is inherently limited by its very nature as a blending of film and interactive media, this is by far the highest quality game of this type to date. While there isn't any compelling gameplay that could stand on its own, the interactivity heightens the story telling for the most part and the detailed and intricate branching paths are meaningful and easy to follow due to the addition of the flowchart.

While obviously not something that will keep you coming back as much as a Skyrim or Battlefield 4, the game offers a fun and engaging experience that even casual family members can participate in. Playing this with friends and family is great and the story is engaging and compelling enough to justify the cost and the time investment it takes to get through some of the more tedious parts.

And besides this, it also doubles as a great tech demo. If you want to put your GPU through its paces and to see some next gen graphics, this is something you'll want to pick up.

Overall: 8.5/10
(Worth around $30 for around 20 hours of gameplay if you backtrack a bit to see different outcomes)

DBH is absolutely phenomenal. Although I disagree with the possibility of the main premise of the tale (namely, Androids becoming human), the manner in which it is told is still quite compelling. A couple elements that contribute to this are advances in motion capture technology and an incredible score that sets the context for each scene.

The unlockable videos impart a sense of the tremendous amount of time that's invested by actors and crew during filming (nevermind post-processing...). I'll likely come back to this in a year or two and play through a different story line.

Side note: I did encounter consistent graphical stuttering in cutscenes halfway through the game. However, this may have been due to incompatibility with newer drivers.

Detroit: Become Human was nothing but one of the best experiences I've ever had. It is less than a game, yet more of one at the same time. The story was beautiful, letting ME choose my own plot twists, and there are so many paths. The cinematography was simply amazing, as was the voice acting and graphics. This game felt like it was released this year, but it was nearly a decade ago; it really deserves more attention. I really enjoyed all 3 of their stories, each one changed my perspective and changed how I thought about my choices for the next character. I ended up being split on both sides, lmao. I would buy it again if I could. "You can't kill me, I'm not alive."

I looooove this story. It beautifully answers the age-old question "what if robots take over the world?". The storytelling is incredible and insanely captivating. I found so many of the game-changing decisions to be very well-thought-out and complex. I really love the replay-ability of this game. I could easily return to it soon and make different choices and play a completely different game. And how can you go wrong with Jesse Williams!?

The story and characters are great. It was easy to get invested in the characters' relationships. I can understand why it got such good reviews on release (for ps4). But I can't recommend the game exclusively because of how poorly it's optimized for PC. Even running medium settings at 1080p there was enough stutter to ruin the experience. This game is from 2018 - An i5-9400 and overclocked 1660 Ti should be able to run this on high settings and get a steady 30+fps but my experience with the game has given me a wildly variable 17-60fps.

Me sorprendió por completo, no esperaba que un juego narrativo me atrapara tanto, pero las decisiones son tan crudas y los momentos tan intensos que realmente te ponen a prueba. La historia es fascinante, con tres androides, tres realidades distintas. Las actuaciones son sobresalientes, los personajes se ven muy vivos, sin ese valle inquietante, y las emociones están convincentemente reflejadas. La ambientación futurista está muy cuidada. Y además, algo que me encantó es la posibilidad de rejugarlo, tomar otras decisiones, y descubrir finales distintos. Una experiencia emocional, con una historia poderosa y decisiones complejas
